title: fix(scripts): the doc-snippet gate's printed build command says it builds a closure, not the tree
body:
Fixes #7795

On an unbuilt tree the gate prints the command that builds what it needs. That command builds a **closure** — the packages the covered documents import, plus their dependency closure — and it said so nowhere, so a reader who ran it got a scoped build and believed they had built the tree. Measured during objectui#7460 on `origin/main` `abdcd189c`: 34 of 40 packages had a `dist/` afterwards, `census.packagesUnbuilt = 2`.

Only the ergonomics half is left. PR #7794 already took away the false red — `check-readme-exports.test.ts` judges per package now and names `census.packagesUnbuilt` itself — and no existing test is touched here.

## What changed (2 files, both under `scripts/`)

- `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` — a new exported `scopedBuildNotice(named, total)`, printed on the precondition path directly under the command block. `analyze()` also returns the `packageDirOf` inventory it had already read; that is where the denominator comes from.
- `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts` — five pins for it.

**The package selection is untouched**: no change to `buildFilterArgs`, to `neededPackages`, or to anything the filter reads. Byte proof below.

## Lit control — the notice on a real unbuilt tree

Nothing was built in this worktree yet, so the precondition path opens on its own. `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`, exit **2**, last six lines of stderr, verbatim:

```text
PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2) — The snippet program was NOT run: the packages it resolves against are not built, or are typed from source.
This is "I could not run", NOT "I ran and found errors" (exit 1). No line above is a verdict about any document, and this run says nothing about whether the documentation compiles. Build what the gate needs, then re-run:
  pnpm exec turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter) --concurrency=2
  pnpm check:doc-snippets

That build is SCOPED, and it is not a whole-tree build: --build-filter names the 26 package(s) the covered documents import (packages/ holds 40) plus each one's dependency closure, and every package outside that closure is left exactly as it was. An unbuilt package still sitting there when the build finishes is this gate's designed end state, not a build that half-failed — building the whole tree for a documentation check would slow every local loop. For the exact set, ask that same filter rather than a list written down somewhere else: append --dry=text to the command above and read its "Packages in scope" line.
```

The same six lines before the change, for comparison — the last two are all the reader used to get:

```text
  packages/types  [unbuilt-package]  @object-ui/types declares types at packages/types/dist/index.d.ts and it is not on disk — run the build first

PRECONDITION NOT MET (exit 2) — The snippet program was NOT run: the packages it resolves against are not built, or are typed from source.
This is "I could not run", NOT "I ran and found errors" (exit 1). No line above is a verdict about any document, and this run says nothing about whether the documentation compiles. Build what the gate needs, then re-run:
  pnpm exec turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter) --concurrency=2
  pnpm check:doc-snippets
```

Both numbers in the new paragraph are the gate's own reading of this tree: **26** is what `--build-filter` names, **40** is what `packages/` holds. Cross-checked against turbo on the same tree, `--dry=text` prints `Running build in 35 packages` and `Packages in scope: …` (26 named + their dependency closure), and the packages under `packages/` it never mentions are `@object-ui/create-plugin`, `@object-ui/plugin-ai`, `@object-ui/plugin-tree`, `@object-ui/runner`, `object-ui` — that number is exactly what the reader can now ask for, and exactly what this PR refuses to write down anywhere.

## The void condition was not tripped — `--build-filter` is byte-identical

```console
$ node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter > filter.before.txt   # before the edit
$ node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter > filter.after.txt    # after
$ diff filter.before.txt filter.after.txt ; echo "diff exit=$?"
diff exit=0
$ md5sum filter.before.txt filter.after.txt
845e14005cecf500866cfa1b2307ec26  filter.before.txt
845e14005cecf500866cfa1b2307ec26  filter.after.txt
```

Same 891 bytes, same 26 `--filter=…` words, same md5.

## Why the notice names no package

Naming "the packages it will not build" exactly means predicting turbo's expansion of that filter, which is not the gate's data: measured here, 26 named grow to 35 selected, and the 5 left out are only knowable from the graph plus which packages define a `build` task. A copy of that answer written into this file is a summary that rots the first time coverage moves. So the notice states what the gate itself read (two counts, both arguments) and delegates the exact set to the same filter, expanded by the same tool that is about to run it: append `--dry=text` to the command already printed above it. A pin keeps a package name from ever appearing in the text.

## Pins — 5 new cases, and both legs of the mutation control red

The file now holds 75 cases (all green). A unit test cannot reach the printed output itself: the path only opens when this repository's own packages are unbuilt, and CI has built them by the time the suite runs — which is why the lit control above is on an unbuilt tree instead. What the pins hold is the part that rots.

| mutation on disk (confirmed by grep, restored by `git checkout HEAD --`) | vitest | which case reds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the `scopedBuildNotice(…)` call removed from the precondition path (`scopedBuildNotice` occurrences 2 to 1) | exit 1, 1 failed / 74 passed | `is printed on the precondition path, not merely defined` |
| the count written down instead of interpolated (`${named} package(s)` to `26 package(s)`) | exit 1, 1 failed / 74 passed | `interpolates the counts it is handed …` |
| restored control | exit 0, 75 passed | — |

After each leg `git diff HEAD` was empty and `git hash-object` matched the HEAD blob `f2d8c70f7…`.

## Gate readings

| command | exit | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm check:doc-snippets` (after building the filter's closure, 34 tasks) | 0 | `Every covered documentation snippet compiles against the built types.` — 456 of 456 blocks judged, 0 failed |
| `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` (unbuilt tree, the lit control) | 2 | precondition path, with the new paragraph |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | 0 | `--listFiles` confirms both edited files are in the program (1 hit each), so this is a reading about them |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 5 suites that name this gate | 0 | 5 files, 324 tests passed |
| `pnpm lint:root` | 0 | 33 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors; the two edited files carry 0 of them |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 | 6357 tracked text files scanned |

`pnpm test` in full and the `Doc Snippet Type Check` workflow are left to CI.

## Changeset — not owed, per the gate rather than per a rule

```text
Compared the working tree with a617bb8d3 (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a manifest whose published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 0 changeset(s) added.
✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.
```

That merge-base line is also the file count for this PR: **2**, recorded against the base this branch was cut from.

## Out of scope, filed rather than fixed here

objectui#7811 — `scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` prints the same unscoped command at two sites (lines 1285 and 1721). Same defect class, but that file is outside this card's declared surface, so it is a separate no-assignee card carrying this shape as its repair direction.
